# ATLAS BRAIN — Prompt Atlas V5 Knowledge Base

> Machine-facing reference. This document is the single source of truth for the V5
> organization of Prompt Atlas and the capabilities of every module. It is written
> to be injected into LLM context (Atlas Advisor, MEAT Journey router, or any
> assistant working on or inside the app). Keep it updated with every release.
>
> Status: V5 TARGET ORGANIZATION. The 4.5 build still shows the legacy categories
> until the V5 reorganization ships.

---

## 1. What Prompt Atlas is

Prompt Atlas is a local desktop studio (Electron + local Node server, port 3783)
for crafting production-grade prompts for AI image and video generation. It is
built from the working experience of a 3D/animation director (Meat Dept). Users
are professional creators: directors, animators, designers. The app ships ~25
specialized modules organized into workshops ("ateliers"), a global AI layer
(OpenAI / Anthropic / DeepSeek / Google Gemini, user-supplied API keys stored
locally), and cross-module routing ("send to" bridges).

Target generation engines the prompts are written for: Kling 3, Seedance 2.0,
Veo 3.x, Midjourney/Flux-class image models, Nano-Banana-class edit models.

---

## 2. Global systems (available everywhere)

### Atlas Advisor
Top of the shell. Free-text need + optional image drop. Routes the user to the
best 1-3 modules and can produce a starter prompt. Uses local keyword scoring +
the selected LLM. THIS DOCUMENT is its knowledge base.

### Global AI selector (topbar)
Two-level choice: provider (OpenAI / Anthropic / DeepSeek / Google Gemini) then
model, each model labeled by intent: Puissant / Equilibre / Economique /
Redaction premium / Rapide / Stable. The choice is broadcast to every module and
the server routes all AI calls accordingly (`/api/ai/*`). DeepSeek has no vision:
image/video analysis must use OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini.

### Settings
API keys for the 4 providers (stored in local `settings.local.json`, never sent
to the page or bundled). Status pill in topbar reflects the selected provider's
key state.

### DECK
Personal pinned workspace: up to 5 modules side-stacked, saveable as named
favorites. Not a category — a user-curated set.

### Grid controls + "Grid to Mov"
For grid-based modules: global columns × rows control. "Grid to Mov" converts a
grid concept into motion prompts (Kling 3 / Seedance 2 / Veo) in three styles:
Narrative (1s clean cuts), Montage (0.7s angles), Storyboard (free, 35mm).

### Send-to bridges (cross-module routing)
- Image Analyzer → A.P.G (intent), CCP, Video Multi Framing (subject/context/style)
- Blocking Studio → Video Multi Framing (trajectory prompt + subject/context/style) and BZ Camera Suite (camera-only move as an extra composite layer)
- FACS Sheet Generator → BZ Board (story or motion acting cues)
- A.P.G / Simple Prompt Builder → other modules via copy/export menus
- BZ Image DNA favorites → copy menu with module targets
- Shell broadcasts: AI model, grid size, theme to every embedded module.

### Skins
Four interface themes, selected by clicking the logo: Rouge Editorial, Noir
Atelier, Mint Blueprint, and La Régie (new in V5). La Régie is the broadcast
control-room skin: dark monitor-lit palette, tally-red accent, VU-meter amber,
prompt/code areas rendered as green phosphor on black with subtle CRT
scanlines. It is the first interactive skin — a topbar console shows a running
25 fps timecode, its tally dot pulses REC while any AI call is in flight
(shell or embedded module), copying a prompt lights a blinking ON AIR badge,
and switching apps or skins flashes a short TV-static transition (cooldown a
few seconds between app switches).

---

## 3. V5 Workshops and modules

Sidebar order = creation pipeline: idea → look → character/asset → boards →
motion → backstage.

### 3.1 IDEA STUDIO — find and shape the idea
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| A.P.G (Absurd Prompt Generator) | Generate original concepts by blending 50 weighted themes |
| Simple Prompt Builder | Assemble prompts from syntactic blocks (subject/action/genre/background/light/camera) |

**A.P.G** — the idea engine.
- Path: Idea Studio → A.P.G.
- 50 theme faders (potards), weight 0-60, max 8 active blended per generation.
  Themes range from canonical (Surrealiste, Kafkaien, Film Noir, Cyberpunk) to
  niche/cultured (Pataphysique, Oulipo, Situationniste, Memphis Milano, Bauhaus,
  Wabi-sabi, Ukiyo-e, Giallo, Nouvelle Vague, Stalker, Metaphysica, Bosch,
  Vanitas, Art Nouveau, Constructiviste, Art Brut, Wunderkammer, Hauntologie,
  Solarpunk, Atompunk, Moebius, Helvetica).
- Weight semantics are a STRICT HIERARCHY enforced server-side: rank-1 theme
  dictates core concept and visual grammar; rank-2 shapes action/styling; lower
  ranks contribute one accent each. Recent outputs travel with each request so
  the model never repeats itself.
- Controls: Intent field (anchor), Output type (image/video), Target engine,
  Complexity 1-10, Absurdity 1-10, Shuffle, Generate (AI), Local seed (offline),
  Guide + regenerate. Transform chips: AI Refine, More realistic, More cinematic,
  More absurd, Cleaner commercial, Darker, Funnier, Editorial, To image, To video.
- History panel keeps the last 80 generations.

**Simple Prompt Builder**
- Path: Idea Studio → Simple Prompt Builder.
- Tabbed banks of cinematic building blocks; click to compose a "verbalized
  prompt"; export menu includes send to Video Multi Framing.

**Image Analyzer** (lives in Backstage)
- Path: Backstage → Image Analyzer.
- Drop an image → vision analysis (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini) → full prompt +
  Seedance-split (subject / context / style) → send to A.P.G, CCP, or VMF.
- Routing note: it remains the natural FIRST STEP of many idea workflows;
  route "I have an image, turn it into a prompt" here even though it sits in
  the toolbox.

### 3.2 LOOK LIBRARY — choose the visual signature
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| BZ Image DNA | ~1500-prompt curated bank: exterior/interior/studio/conceptual + Photo DNA add-ons (camera, film, lighting) |
| BZ Realism Forge v2 | Simulate capture origin: device realism (Disposable, Polaroid, Early Century, Film SLR, Compact Digital, Smartphone, Webcam/Surveillance, Camcorder, TV/Tube) |
| BZ Beauty | Portrait/skin realism compiler: Selfie, Portrait, Skin Realism, Lighting, Negatives tabs; Femme/Homme toggle |
| BZ Goodies | 70 era-styled looks, 1930s → 2000s, plus fun transformations |
| BZ Enhancer | Prompt-based repair/refinement of the look: surgical fixes, hand/anatomy, face polish, detail sharpen, style lock, cinematic grade, artifact cleanup, quick fix; Angles 3×3; Render Pass |

Notes for routing: "make it look like a 1990s camcorder" → Realism Forge.
"believable skin, anti-AI portrait" → BZ Beauty. "1950s atmosphere" → BZ Goodies.
"fashion/editorial photo direction" → BZ Image DNA. Each Realism Forge tab has
Subject & Scene fields (personality, outfit, pose, location, expression) applied
to every prompt; "FOOL GEMINI" pill = anti-AI-detection flavor.

### 3.3 CHARACTER & ASSET LAB — build and lock references
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| BZ Designer | Sketch-to-photo/clay/manga/comics conversion with Original Drawing Weight slider (20-95%), body construction, puppet integration, production shortcuts |
| BZ Sheet | Tech boards and character reference sheets (Tech Board / Character Sheet tabs), background color swatches, per-prompt info popups |
| CCP (Consistent Character Processus) | Step-based pipeline: Contact Sheet 2.0 (3×3, 9 views), Character Sheet professional reference (7 views), Storyboard Sequence; the identity-locking workflow |
| Knolling Board Generator | Generate Knolling Board / Knolling Tattoo / Actor Extract / Extract Decor; Lighting Mode (Original vs Diffuse); Puppet/Human toggle |
| 2D/3D Transfer | Pose Transfer Lab: 2D prompt cards + 3D image/video transfer modes, blocking-oriented |

Routing notes: "keep my character identical across images" → CCP. "turn my
sketch into a finished image but keep my drawing" → BZ Designer (set Drawing
Weight high). "extract the actor/decor from this image into a flat-lay
reference" → Knolling. "orthographic product sheet" → BZ Sheet Object Sheet.

### 3.4 BOARD & SEQUENCE — boards, grids, découpage
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Cinematic Shoot | Theme-organized cinematic grid prompts with per-prompt AI iteration |
| BZ Multishot | Camera angles, multishot sequences, action boards for reference grids |
| BZ Board | Storyboard → Motion two-step pipeline with [IMG_1..6] reference slots, FACS acting-cue inbox, local GPT refinement |

Grid controls + Grid to Mov apply here. Routing: "contact sheet of camera
angles" → BZ Multishot. "build a storyboard then make it move" → BZ Board.

### 3.5 MOTION STUDIO — direct movement and performance
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Video Multi Framing | Stills or Moving sequences from image refs; Kling timed wording or Seedance cut-to wording; up to 30 shots / 15s; director templates (Standard, Fincher, Noé, Burton, Wong Kar-wai, Lanthimos); ACTION DIRECTION + GO ACTION = AI stages the shots around the user's direction (escalation, cause-effect, continuity) |
| Acting Gen | Video prompt library for physical performance: tabs ACTION / EMOTION / VFX / DANCE. Action categories: Sport, Gun, Daily, Interaction, Violence, Fly, Dance, Vehicle, Supernatural. The DANCE tab hosts the full Drunk Dance collection (8 categories × 20 prompts, original architecture preserved, loaded at runtime from its source file) |
| FACS Sheet Generator | Facial Action Units → expression sheets or acting layers; send cues to BZ Board (story/motion) |

Routing notes: "I have a video, give me the prompt that recreates/redirects it"
→ Video Director Analyzer (Backstage). "stage a fight scene across 7 shots" →
Video Multi Framing MOVING MODE → type Action direction → GO ACTION.
"drunk/comedy dance performance" → Acting Gen DANCE tab.

### 3.6 CAMERA CONTROL — lens, movement, texture
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| BZ Camera Suite | Camera motion / optics / film-stock toggles compositing one video prompt (Dolly/Track, Steadicam, Crane/Jib, Whip Pan, Static, Handheld...) with intensity sliders |
| Imperfection Engine | UGC realism: human micro-motion, camera imperfection, anti-sterile video |

Routing notes: "camera language only" → BZ Camera Suite. "make it feel
handheld/amateur/real" → Imperfection Engine.

### 3.7 BACKSTAGE — prep, cut, fix (the toolbox)
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Image Analyzer | Turn any image into a structured prompt (vision), then route it to A.P.G, CCP or VMF |
| Image Slicer | Slice grids/sheets into individual images, optional .zip |
| Paint Studio | Annotate images: draw, text, layers, erasers, export PNG (fluidity/style overhaul planned) |
| Image Graber | Scrub any video, export exact frame as PNG |
| Video Director Analyzer | Drop a video (≤15s window, IN/OUT trim) → frame+transcript analysis → director breakdown + ready Kling 3 prompt + negative + Seedance 2.0 paragraph; export MP3/black MP4; downloads menu. Functionally belongs to Motion Studio: route motion-analysis requests here |
| Blocking Studio | Three.js 3D previz stage (local, offline, vendored Three.js r170). Posable low-poly mannequins (~13 FK joints, 8 pose presets: T-pose/Stand/Walk/Run/Sit/Crouch/Point/Lie, renameable — names flow into labels, HUD and wording); the +Mannequin button opens a menu to add the native mannequin OR instantiate any saved Mixamo/GLB character from the library, which then behaves as a poseable character (pose presets + Pose Library + FACS all apply to rigged GLB bipeds), set primitives (box, wall, cylinder, sphere, ramp, table), draggable key-light sun with cinematographic verbalization (azimuth, elevation and a 0–300% Intensity slider that scales the key light and the lighting wording), 1m ground grid. MULTI-CAMERA: any number of cameras, each renameable with an assigned color (colored body + frustum), active-camera chips selector; the LENS view, timeline, exports and wording all follow the active camera. Each camera owns a draggable look-at TARGET (sphere+cross marker, shown in Scout/Split, hidden in Lens) — dragging it re-aims the camera, otherwise it tracks the look-point; target pos/distance persist with the scene. Real lenses: full-frame sensor, 24/35/50/85mm, aspects 16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 / 2.39, three views — SCOUT (orbit + frustums, Blender-style axis-orb navigation gizmo with view snapping, Alt/Shift+drag pan, wheel zoom), LENS (through-the-lens, letterboxed, thirds; drag pan/tilt, Alt/Shift+drag truck, wheel dolly, WASD) and SPLIT (scout left + active lens right). Click-to-select AND the transform gizmo work in every view (both split half-viewports and the lens — the gizmo retargets to the camera that renders the region). Gizmo shortcuts R/P/S (rotate/move/scale) and a right-click viewport menu (Rotate/Position/Scale · Gizmo World/Local toggle · Scout/Lens/Split). UNDO/REDO (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z, 30-step stack covering moves, rotations, poses and object add/delete) — reference-holding snapshots restore the real GLB/mannequin objects (delete only detaches, never disposes), commits debounced on the autosave timer. Scale applies to props and full characters — including native mannequins (selecting a limb/joint then Scale scales the whole figure). A topbar ⛶ button toggles real fullscreen (requestFullscreen). Optional depth-of-field preview in Lens view (camera-panel DOF toggle + focus-distance and bokeh sliders, BokehPass postprocessing then an OutputPass for correct sRGB/tone-mapping so DOF doesn't darken the frame, all vendored). Any character — a mannequin OR a rigged GLB — can be the framing subject. Live HUD classifies shot size (ECU→EWS) and angle (low/eye/high + frontal/3-4/profile/back) against the marked subject. Per-camera move timeline (multi-key, 1-15s, ease, play preview; keyframe chips are draggable to retime them, giving per-segment shot durations) with local-rules wording generator (dolly/truck/crane/arc/pan/tilt/zoom/dolly-zoom + speed) and an "Export MP4" that records the camera move to video over the timeline duration (MediaRecorder; H.264 MP4 when the runtime supports it, WebM fallback). Character name ANNOTATIONS are DOM/canvas bubbles with a leader arrow pointing at each character, clamped to the viewport edges so they stay on-screen and readable even in close-ups (and pointing toward off-screen subjects); they are drawn into snapshots when Clean plate is off (now the default). Exports: viewport snapshot PNG (clean-plate toggle for image-to-image reference, default off so annotations show; optional caption burn-in), camera description text, trajectory wording in Kling 3 / Seedance 2.0 / camera-only formats with optional AI Polish (`/api/ai/refine`, global model). Send-to: Video Multi Framing (subject/context/style) and BZ Camera Suite (camera-only line as composite layer). AI-RENDER PIPELINE: model import — GLB/GLTF and FBX (vendored GLTFLoader + FBXLoader, fully offline; file input or drag-drop; container sniffed from the bytes, not the filename; auto-scaled and grounded; GLB recommended; restored as labeled placeholders from saved scenes since binaries are not embedded) plus a favorites LIBRARY (metadata + auto thumbnail in localStorage, bytes in IndexedDB; drop/picker to save, click to instantiate, Manage to rename/delete); rigged models (GLB or FBX with SkinnedMesh + Skeleton) are auto-detected — bones listed in the rail under the object, click a bone (rail or viewport marker) for an FK rotation gizmo, and biped rigs (Mixamo-style name heuristic: Hips/Spine/Head/Arm/ForeArm/UpLeg/Leg…) get the 8 pose presets applied as world-axis bone rotations pre-multiplied in parent space then re-skinned so the mesh deforms (FK only, no IK); a POSE LIBRARY saves the current rig pose as a favorite (auto thumbnail + canonical-bone deltas from bind, persisted in IndexedDB) and re-applies it to any Mixamo biped in the scene — poses are interoperable across characters because they are stored per canonical bone; rename/delete via Manage; per-character FACS expression popup (49 Action Units from the FACS Sheet Generator bank, same yellow-face card graphics) for native mannequins AND rigged GLBs — the chosen expression is shown as a gently-curved Three.js face-card plane on the head (native neck joint or the Head/mixamorig:Head bone) in two modes — "Billboard" (always faces the camera) or "3D" (locked to the head, follows its translation+rotation, hand-orientable with the rotate gizmo when selected) — needs no UV mapping so it works on any rig, and feeds the wording ("Performance:" line), the AI Render prompt and the storyboard prompt; "AI Render" panel translates the current blocking (characters, poses, expressions, set, light, camera) into an image-render prompt (local rules + AI Polish) with a style-preset menu (Cinematic / Concept / Storyboard ink / Photoreal golden-hour / Noir / Animation); SHOT DECK: "Snapshot to deck" collects clean-plate frames with camera metadata, a per-shot duration slider (default 2s) and an editable dialogue field; "Export storyboard + prompt" outputs the snapshot grid PNG plus a scene-nomenclature prompt with [IMG_n] reference tags ([IMG_1] = blocking grid, one tag per named character sheet, one for the decor reference) with dialogue integrated shot by shot; "Export deck MP4" assembles the snapshots into a video honoring each shot's duration (dialogue burned in as a lower-third). Scene autosaves to localStorage + JSON export/import (v2 format, v1 migrated; deck and expressions included). In the shell it opens fullscreen (fills the content column, like Paint Studio) |

Routing notes: "block/previz a scene in 3D before generating", "which focal length /
lens should I frame this with", "design a camera move and get the Kling/Seedance
wording", "I need a posable mannequin reference image", "turn my 3D blocking into
a storyboard grid + render prompt", "import my GLB model into the previz" →
Blocking Studio. Its clean-plate PNG is made to be dropped into VMF IMG slots or
any image-to-image engine as a composition reference; the shot-deck storyboard
prompt expects the user's character sheets (CCP) and decor grids as [IMG_n] inputs.

---

## 4. Recipes (multi-module workflows)

**Sketch → locked character → board → video**
1. BZ Designer (Sketch to Image, set Drawing Weight) → finished character image.
2. CCP Contact Sheet 2.0 → 9-view identity lock; Character Sheet for reference.
3. BZ Board: place [IMG] refs, write beats; FACS Generator → send acting cues.
4. BZ Board step 2 (Motion) or Video Multi Framing with IMG drops → video prompt.

**Image → restyled video sequence**
1. Image Analyzer (or VMF IMG DROP) → subject/context/style filled.
2. Look Library pass (Realism Forge or Image DNA) to set the visual signature.
3. VMF MOVING MODE: duration, shots, Action direction → GO ACTION → Kling/Seedance.

**Existing video → new subject, same direction**
1. Video Director Analyzer: drop video, trim window, set Required subject change.
2. Output: Kling prompt + negative, or Seedance paragraph. Refine in VMF if needed.

**Idea from nothing**
1. A.P.G: pick 2-3 themes (one dominant), set intent if any → Generate.
2. Transform chips (More cinematic / To video) → send onward.

**Blocking → motion (previz a camera move before generating)**
1. Blocking Studio: place mannequins (pose presets) + set primitives, aim the key light.
2. Pick focal/aspect, frame in LENS view, add 2-8 camera keys on the timeline, Play to check.
3. Export: clean-plate PNG (image-to-image reference) + camera description text.
4. Trajectory wording (Kling or Seedance, AI Polish optional) → send to Video Multi
   Framing for staging, or camera-only line → BZ Camera Suite to stack optics/film layers.

**Grid → motion**
1. Any Board & Sequence module with grid → "Grid to Mov" (pick engine + style).

---

## 5. Server API (for integrations)

Local only, 127.0.0.1:3783. Key endpoints:
- `GET /api/settings` — key states, selected model, `llmModels` registry.
- `POST /api/settings` — save keys (`openaiApiKey`, `anthropicApiKey`,
  `deepseekApiKey`, `googleApiKey`), `llmModel`.
- `POST /api/ai/refine` — { prompt, transform, intent, outputType, model }.
- `POST /api/ai/compose` — A.P.G semantic mix { intent, blend[], complexity,
  absurdity, recentOutputs[], localDraft }.
- `POST /api/ai/analyze-image` — { imageDataUrl, model } → prompt + seedance split.
- `POST /api/ai/analyze-video` — { frames[], duration, transcript, direction }
  → analysis + klingPrompt + klingNegativePrompt + seedancePrompt.
- `POST /api/ai/transcribe-video` — OpenAI Whisper only.
- `POST /api/media/*` — ffmpeg exports (audio, frames).
All AI endpoints route through the multi-provider layer; missing key → clear
per-provider error; analysis falls back to local generation with a warning note.

---

## 6. Roadmap context (V5+)

- **V5**: this reorganization + "La Régie" interactive skin (shipped) +
  Blocking Studio module (shipped) + Advisor powered by this document (`GET /api/brain`).
- **V5 follow-ups**: promote Video Director Analyzer out of the Backstage panel
  into a standalone Motion Studio module; move BZ Enhancer card from Look
  Library to Backstage once the panel supports module cards; Paint Studio
  overhaul (stroke smoothing, pressure, better toolset, modern feel).
  (Done in 5.0.x: Drunk Dance merged into Acting Gen as the DANCE tab; SFX tab
  renamed VFX; Camera Control workshop created; injected info buttons fixed so
  they open the info panel instead of triggering the card copy.)
- **MEAT Journey**: image/video generation aggregator built on fal.ai API
  (Phase 1 = BYOK fal key, Generate buttons beside prompts, local gallery).
  Prompt Atlas becomes its integrated prompt-crafting brain. Naming: play on
  Midjourney × Meat Dept.

## 7. Maintenance rules

- Any new module MUST be added here: workshop, purpose, path, functions, bridges.
- Any renamed workshop/module updates sections 3-4 and the Advisor wiring.
- Model registry changes (providers, ids, labels) update section 2.
- Keep routing notes ("user says X → module Y") rich: they are what makes the
  Advisor feel intelligent.

rigged models (GLB or FBX with SkinnedMesh + Skeleton) are auto-detected — bones listed in the rail under the object, click a bone (rail or viewport marker) for an FK rotation gizmo, and biped rigs (Mixamo-style name heuristic: Hips/Spine/Head/Arm/ForeArm/UpLeg/Leg…) get the 8 pose presets applied as world-axis bone rotations pre-multiplied in parent space then re-skinned so the mesh deforms (FK only, no IK); a POSE LIBRARY saves the current rig pose as a favorite (auto thumbnail + canonical-bone deltas from bind, persisted in IndexedDB) and re-applies it to any Mixamo biped in the scene — poses are interoperable across characters because they are stored per canonical bone; rename/delete via Manage; per-character FACS expression popup (49 Action Units from the FACS Sheet Generator bank, same yellow-face card graphics) for native mannequins AND rigged GLBs — the chosen expression is shown as a gently-curved Three.js face-card plane on the head (native neck joint or the Head/mixamorig:Head bone) in two modes — "Billboard" (always faces the camera) or "3D" (locked to the head, follows its translation+rotation, hand-orientable with the rotate gizmo when selected) — needs no UV mapping so it works on any rig, and feeds the wording ("Performance:" line), the AI Render prompt and the storyboard prompt; "Export deck MP4" assembles the snapshots into a video honoring each shot's duration (dialogue burned in as a lower-third). Scene autosaves to localStorage + JSON export/import (v2 format, v1 migrated; deck and expressions included). In the shell it opens fullscreen (fills the content column, like Paint Studio) |

## 4. Recipes (multi-module workflows)

**Sketch → locked character → board → video**
1. BZ Designer (Sketch to Image, set Drawing Weight) → finished character image.
2. CCP Contact Sheet 2.0 → 9-view identity lock; Character Sheet for reference.
3. BZ Board: place [IMG] refs, write beats; FACS Generator → send acting cues.
4. BZ Board step 2 (Motion) or Video Multi Framing with IMG drops → video prompt.

**Image → restyled video sequence**
1. Image Analyzer (or VMF IMG DROP) → subject/context/style filled.
2. Look Library pass (Realism Forge or Image DNA) to set the visual signature.
3. VMF MOVING MODE: duration, shots, Action direction → GO ACTION → Kling/Seedance.

**Existing video → new subject, same direction**
1. Video Director Analyzer: drop video, trim window, set Required subject change.
2. Output: Kling prompt + negative, or Seedance paragraph. Refine in VMF if needed.

**Idea from nothing**
1. A.P.G: pick 2-3 themes (one dominant), set intent if any → Generate.
2. Transform chips (More cinematic / To video) → send onward.

**Blocking → motion (previz a camera move before generating)**
1. Blocking Studio: place mannequins (pose presets) + set primitives, aim the key light.
2. Pick focal/aspect, frame in LENS view, add 2-8 camera keys on the timeline, Play to check.
3. Export: clean-plate PNG (image-to-image reference) + camera description text.
4. Trajectory wording (Kling or Seedance, AI Polish optional) → send to Video Multi
   Framing for staging, or camera-only line → BZ Camera Suite to stack optics/film layers.

**Grid → motion**
1. Any Board & Sequence module with grid → "Grid to Mov" (pick engine + style).

## 5. Server API (for integrations)

Local only, 127.0.0.1:3783. Key endpoints:
- `GET /api/settings` — key states, selected model, `llmModels` registry.
- `POST /api/settings` — save keys (`openaiApiKey`, `anthropicApiKey`,
  `deepseekApiKey`, `googleApiKey`), `llmModel`.
- `POST /api/ai/refine` — { prompt, transform, intent, outputType, model }.
- `POST /api/ai/compose` — A.P.G semantic mix { intent, blend[], complexity,
  absurdity, recentOutputs[], localDraft }.
- `POST /api/ai/analyze-image` — { imageDataUrl, model } → prompt + seedance split.
- `POST /api/ai/analyze-video` — { frames[], duration, transcript, direction }
  → analysis + klingPrompt + klingNegativePrompt + seedancePrompt.
- `POST /api/ai/transcribe-video` — OpenAI Whisper only.
- `POST /api/media/*` — ffmpeg exports (audio, frames).
All AI endpoints route through the multi-provider layer; missing key → clear
per-provider error; analysis falls back to local generation with a warning note.
